title: The 5 Largest Deserts on Earth, Ranked (#1 Has No Sand at All)

scenes.text: The five biggest deserts on Earth, ranked. Number one has no sand and almost no heat.

scenes.label: Gobi · 0.5M sq mi
scenes.text: Number five: the Gobi. About half a million square miles of cold, rocky desert across China and Mongolia.

scenes.label: Arabian · 1.0M sq mi
scenes.text: Number four: the Arabian Desert. About one million square miles, covering most of the Arabian Peninsula.

scenes.label: Sahara · 3.5M sq mi
scenes.text: Number three: the Sahara. About three and a half million square miles, nearly the size of the United States.

scenes.label: Arctic · 5.4M sq mi
scenes.text: Number two: the Arctic. About five and a half million square miles of ice and frozen ground.

scenes.label: Antarctica · 5.5M sq mi
scenes.text: Number one: Antarctica. About five and a half million square miles, with under half an inch of precipitation a year. It is a desert.

description:
The five largest deserts on Earth, ranked by area.
A desert is defined by how little rain or snow falls, not by heat, so the biggest one is a frozen continent.
Which would you cross?
first_comment: Did you think the Sahara was number one? What should we rank next?
